sources.title: A Parallel Distributed Cognitive Control System for a Humanoid Robot
sources.access: University-hosted publisher PDF, selected pp.65–68,79–81,88 text; pp.65 and 88 visually verified; publisher copyright

implemented: Distributed physical robot controller; reported acquisition and interpolation of motion sequences from demonstration; fault detection results in simulation.
learned: Motion vocabulary from recorded human-guided trajectories and derived combinations.
designed: Hardware, feature extractors, controllers, segmentation heuristics, memory and user-defined interpolation space.
limit: Human teleoperation and some manual segmentation; distributed communications scalability and lockups reported; adaptive working memory still being explored at p.88.
ora: Distinguish acquired motor composition from scaffolding and distinguish increasing module count from increased reliable capacity.

sources.title: Modeling the Mechanisms of Emotion Effects on Cognition
sources.access: Publisher PDF, first page visually verified; selected text; AAAI copyright

sources.title: Reasons for Emotions: Modeling Emotions in Integrated Cognitive Systems

implemented: Symbolic affect-dependent processing model; author reports distinct simulated decision patterns and ongoing human validation in 2008.
learned: No autonomous development of affect mechanisms established in inspected sources.
designed: Parameters for capacity, speed, bias and appraisal; domain knowledge and modeler tuning.
limit: Simulation of emotion effects is not evidence of subjective emotion; alternative parameterizations can explain observed behavior.
ora: A state-dependent behavioral change does not prove a new internally learned mechanism.

implemented: Virtual interactive character with affective state driving expression and cognitive functions; reported card-game user perception study.
learned: Persistent autonomous cognitive learning not established by these abstracts.
designed: Affect coordinates, reasoning and expressive mappings; simulated embodiment.
limit: Reported human judgments of character age are observer responses, not evidence of felt emotion or development of cognition.
ora: Separate externally perceived lifelikeness from internal mechanism acquisition.

sources.authors: Francisco Bellas; Richard J. Duro; Andrés Faiña; Daniel Souto
sources.title: Multilevel Darwinist Brain (MDB): Artificial Evolution in a Cognitive Architecture for Real Robots
sources.access: University-hosted indexed publisher PDF, selected sections II–IV text; page image retrieval HTTP 404; IEEE copyright

implemented: Author reports online neuroevolution of models and behaviors on physical robots; hexapod gait and induced behavior on AIBO and Pioneer 2.
learned: Predictive models and behavior parameters from interaction; reported reuse of models when an earlier teacher command mapping returned.
designed: Evolutionary optimizer, model classes, sensory/action representation and satisfaction maximization; teacher rewards or task distance define evaluation.
limit: First gait experiment uses human resets after falls/lost target, no LTM, no internal sensing; teacher-guided examples use external reward. Populations are candidate models/behaviors inside a robot, not reproducing metabolically bounded organisms. No E3.
ora: High-value comparator for within-lifetime evolutionary learning vs between-organism inheritance and resource-funded viability; no novelty claim.

ora: Separate emergent interaction of authored modules from acquired cognitive competencies.
